controls.notesEn: Popup opens below the field with a check mark on the current item. Windows 26.0 lists the same 11 codes in another order. Only the key cap labels change.

Mac 26.2.1 lists 12 items (Windows 26.0 also had 'App'). Panels are alphabetical after a separator. Choosing a panel: the keyboard shows only that panel's shortcuts (solid green; everything else grey, no application colours) and the tree shows that panel's group expanded at the top. Choosing Application returns to the mixed colouring.

layoutMac.units: pt, dialog-local; key height 60 unless given; pitch 65
layoutMac.notesEn: No Esc, Help, Insert, F13+ or Clear key on the Mac keyboard drawing (Esc and Clear (Num) still appear in the command tree). Key names wrap (Forward / Delete, Page / Down, Enter / (Num)).

keyCap.commandName: top-left, white, up to two lines, truncated with '...'

applicationScope.panelOnly: grey upper-left triangle, green lower-right triangle (diagonal from bottom-left to top-right), no label
applicationScope.both: purple upper-left triangle, green lower-right triangle, label = application command

keyCap.panelScope: keys bound in the chosen panel are solid green with the panel command's name; all others solid grey
keyCap.modifierKeys: Caps Lock, Shift, Ctrl, Opt, Cmd are darker grey (#636363); a pressed modifier (both copies) is blue (#0071ca)
keyCap.selected: blue 1-pt outline (#4ea9f6) on the clicked key

modifiers.click: clicking a modifier key cap toggles it (sticky); several combine (Cmd then Shift = ⇧⌘ layer). Click again to release.
modifiers.hold: holding the physical modifier shows the same layer while held (both copies blue) and returns when released
modifiers.display: with modifiers active every key shows the command bound to that modifier combination (colours as above)

hover.tooltip: one line per assignment: '<Scope>: <Command> (<Path> → … → <Command>)', e.g. 'Application: Show/Hide Properties with Keyframes (Double-Tap) (Application → Animation → Show/Hide Properties with Keyframes (Double-Tap))'; a key with an application and a panel command lists both ('Character and Paragraph Panels: Backspace (Previous Character) (Panels → Character and Paragraph Panels → Backspace (Previous Character))')

controls.click: selects the key (outline) and fills the Key table on the right
controls.drop: dragging a command row from the tree onto a key cap assigns that key with the active modifiers to the command (added to its existing shortcuts). Observed: Composition Settings dropped on F5 → F5 became purple/green with label 'Composition Settings', Key: F5 (multiple commands assigned) listed 'Show Snapshot 1' and 'Composition Settings' as pills; no conflict message because F5 had only a panel command.

controls.notesEn: 14-pt squares with text, one line under the keyboard at x 33 / 368 / 775.

Magnifier icon, no placeholder, focused when the dialog opens (blue ring). Typing filters the tree live; matching rows are shown with their groups expanded (search 'composition settings' → Application ▸ Composition ▸ Composition Settings ⌘+K). An × clear button appears while it has text. The keyboard does not change. Making a change in the tree cleared the search.

controls.structure: Application: 27 tool commands first (no group), then one group per menu in menu order (File, Edit, Composition, Layer, Effect, Animation, View, Window; submenus are nested groups; no After Effects / Help menu groups), then ~55 commands that are in no menu (Cancel Preview, Help, Preferences, Quit, Switch to Workspace #1 …). Panels: one group per panel scope, alphabetical. See commandTreeGroups.
controls.expansion: chevron › / ⌄ left of each group; clicking the group row toggles it. Initially Application and Panels are expanded, their groups collapsed.
controls.rowLook: 33-pt rows, black (#101010) background with 1-pt separators; group rows have the chevron; command rows are indented one step per level (≈ 23 pt).

shortcutCell.unselectedRow: plain text, chords joined by ', ' ('⌘+N, ⌘+K', 'Return, Enter (Num)')
shortcutCell.selectedRow: each chord is a pill: rounded outline, chord text, × button; the focused pill has a blue ring
shortcutCell.firstClick: clicking anywhere in the Shortcut cell selects the row and focuses its first pill (Clear becomes enabled)
shortcutCell.secondClickOnEmptyArea: adds an empty pill (only ×) with the blue ring, waiting for a key press
shortcutCell.keyPress: the pressed chord (with its modifiers) is assigned at once; the new pill appears after the existing ones; the ring moves back to the first pill

behaviorLog: Open: preset After Effects Default.txt, Commands Application, search focused, Key: empty, Delete and Undo and Clear disabled.

Commands → Timeline Panel: keyboard solid green for timeline shortcuts (Zoom Out on -, Zoom In on =, Show/Hide … on E R T A S F, Go to Previous / Next Keyframe on J K, Set Work Area Start / End on B N, Open Composition on \, Select Layer by Number on numpad 1–9, Open Layer Source in Layer Panel on Return / Enter (Num) …), everything else grey; tree shows Timeline Panel expanded.
Click K: outline on K; Key: K (multiple commands assigned) with 16 modifier rows.

Click ⌘ key cap: both ⌘ caps blue, every key shows its ⌘ command (Show/Hide Tools … on 1–0, Quit Q, Close Current … W, Composition Settings K, Undo Last Action Z …); then ⇧ too → ⇧⌘ layer. Clicking again releases.
Click pill × on Composition Settings ⌘+K: shortcut removed, preset switches to Custom.txt (Delete enabled), search cleared, Undo enabled.
Undo: ⌘+K back as the focused pill, Undo disabled, preset stays Custom.txt.
New Composition: click Shortcut cell → ⌘+N pill focused; click the empty area again → empty pill; press ⌘K → pills ⌘+N, ⌘+K; Composition Settings loses ⌘+K; warning bar with link.
Click the link: Composition Settings row selected; New Composition row back to plain text '⌘+N, ⌘+K'.
Undo: New Composition ⌘+N only, Composition Settings ⌘+K again, bar empty.
Drag Composition Settings onto F5: F5 assigned (see visual_keyboard.drop).
Save As...: Create Preset dialog, cancelled.
Preset dropdown now lists After Effects Default.txt, ✓ Custom.txt.

presetFiles.builtIn: After Effects Default.txt (read-only in the dialog: Delete disabled)
presetFiles.format: Text, CR line endings. Header comment block ('# Text File Version 1.1', '# After Effects Shortcut Preferences (modify at your own risk)', key identifier list), then sections ["<context class>"] with lines "<CommandId>" = "(<chord>)(<chord>)" (e.g. "NewComp" = "(Cmd+N)", empty "()" = no shortcut; modifiers Cmd, Option, Shift, macControl; keys like PadMultiply, FwdDel, PageUP, SingleQuote).
presetFiles.customWrittenAtOnce: Editing the built-in preset makes AE create aeks/Custom.txt on disk immediately (before OK). Cancel / Escape does not remove it. AE also writes the full table there, normalised (in the incident the coordinator found 25 differences against the default, including duplicate chords dropped). The current preset is stored in Prefs.txt as 'Shortcut File Location' when AE quits.
presetFiles.incident: 2026-11-24: this observation created aeks/Custom.txt; the coordinator moved it out of aeks/. Do not edit anything in this dialog on a user's AE.

clipboardFormat.lineEnding: \r (CR), the text ends with an extra empty line (\r\r)
clipboardFormat.line: <depth × \t><Name>\t<Shortcuts>\t\r — groups have an empty Shortcuts field ('Application\t\t\r', '\tFile\t\t\r'); commands with no shortcut too ('\t\tClose Project\t\t\r')
clipboardFormat.shortcuts: chord texts as in the tree, joined by ', ' ('\tAudio Preview (Here Forward)\t⌃+., Forward Delete (Num), , (Num), . (Num)\t\r')
clipboardFormat.scope: the whole tree (Application then Panels) in tree order, whatever the search, scope or expansion
sample: \t\tOpen Layer Source in Layer Panel\tReturn, Enter (Num)\t
